evals.prompt:
Run a grilling session with these arguments:

issue: none
topic: this request: "Add a CSV export of the monthly report. I have not decided who the file is for (managers who open it in a spreadsheet, or the accounting system that imports it), whether it includes the archived rows, and what the column headers are: the options for the headers depend on who the file is for, but the choice stays open either way."

There is no AskUserQuestion tool in this session, so ask with the numbered list. Play the whole session in this one reply: after each question write my answer on its own line as `> user: <answer>` and go on from there. I answer the first question with "1", every later question with "tak", and the closing menu with "1".
evals.expected_output: The agent announces the size (medium) before any question and says once that the notes stay in chat. It asks one decision per question, starting with who the file is for; each question offers two or three numbered options with a pro/con line, the recommended one first. "1" and "tak" pick the recommendation. The column-header question comes after the answer about who the file is for and builds on it. After every answer it prints a one-line summary and a compact Resolved/Next note, not a full `## Grill state` block. It ends with the full block, a briefing in the conversation language (what the request is, with a concrete example, why the open choices matter, what will be built, what is left out), then the decisions, each named by what it is about, with docs-discipline tags, and a three-option closing menu (act on it, change something, add something not yet discussed).
assertions: Before the first question the agent states the size classification (small, medium or large) and what follows from it, in a way the user can override
The agent says once that with `issue: none` the notes stay in chat and cannot be picked up from another machine
Every question asks exactly one decision; no message between two user answers asks two decisions
Every question offers two or three numbered options, each with one line on what speaks for it or what it costs, and the first option is marked as recommended
No question is a yes/no question; each asks the user to choose between concrete options
The answers "1" and "tak" are each applied as the recommended option of the one question they answer
The column-header question is asked only after the answer about who the file is for, and its options or recommendation take that answer into account

After every answer to a decision the agent prints a one-line summary of what was just decided followed by a compact note with short Resolved bullets and the next question's header, and does not print a full `## Grill state` block between questions
A full `## Grill state` block is printed at the end of the session (or when the notes are requested), and no such block carries a counter field numbering the questions asked so far
No `## Grill state` block is written before the first answer arrives
The outcome opens with a briefing for a fellow developer in the conversation language: what happened with a concrete example, the cause, what will change and what is deliberately left out
After the briefing the outcome lists each decision, named by what it is about, with its answer and a docs-discipline tag (ADR, glossary term, entity-page decision or none)
The confirmation is a menu of three options (act on it as the recommended one, change something, add something not yet discussed), not a yes/no question

None of the internal phrases (frontier, round or runda, fold in, resolved branch, carrier, state block or blok stanu, recommendation accepted, question numbers such as Q3, acceptance-criterion positions such as criterion 6) appears in any text addressed to the user: questions, summary lines, the outcome or the confirmation menu
